tasks.commitBody:
Mihkel asked for the invite link to copy on click. The copy machinery existed — copyLink() with visible failure and a readonly input that stays manually copyable — so the work was the trigger and, more importantly, the confirmation: the success cue lived in the copy button's own label, which stops working the moment a second trigger exists, and a label swap on an element the user did not touch is no announcement at all for a screen reader.

Clicking the readonly input now selects its text and runs the same copyLink() the button uses — one path, one set of failure semantics; the selection is the manual fallback made easy exactly where the automatic path fails by design (no clipboard in non-secure contexts). The confirmation moves to its own persistent role=status region in the #267/#323-328 idiom: mounted from first render, blank until it has something to say, text set on settle, cleared at the start of the next attempt and by create-another, no timer — its own node, never folded into the failure alert, which keeps its insertion-announced role=alert semantics untouched. The button stays as the discoverable affordance and the keyboard path, its label now static.

No navigation was removed — the link was never an anchor. No new strings: the existing copied/copy/copy-error keys serve, in all four locales. The clipboard test infrastructure is new to the tree: payload-asserting success mocks and a genuinely absent writeText for the fallback shape.

Closes #345

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)
